messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT: Pager triggered for service=redwood-runtime-prod, symptom=container crashloop, scope=eu-west-1, severity=sev2. Pager: oncall-eric.

oncall-eric: I see a spike of `CrashLoopBackOff` on the vLLM pod group in eu-west-1, ~120 pods restarting over the last 6m. Customer error rate + dropdown on model-inference SLOs.

alex-ramirez: confirming. kube events show repeated segfaults in the runtime process, container exits with signal 11. Pod logs contain a TensorRT/ CUDA stack trace followed by `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'`.

maya-k: attaching clipped logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:01:23Z] runtime: loading model xfl/7b
[2026-03-15T12:01:25Z] tensorRT: building engine for batch=1
[2026-03-15T12:01:27Z] cuda: cuCtxCreate -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
[2026-03-15T12:01:27Z] runtime: segfault at 0x0 ip=0x7f2c3a1b4d tf
```

trent: nvdriver logs on the host show `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 31` followed by driver recovery. Could be a device memory corruption or illegal access from our fused kernel.

sre-jun: Quick status: impact - ~30% of EU inference traffic getting 5xx / retry fallback to older model variant. Some customers reported timeouts but no data leakage reported. CS notified.

customer-success-lee: we're getting inbound messages from two enterprise customers with requests failing in EU region. They're asking for ETA. I'll keep them updated and escalate if needed.

runtime-ops: Reproduced on a repro node with a smaller model. When we run the same config with TensorRT fused kernels enabled we get a deterministic segfault within 15s. With `--tensorrt-disable-fusion` it stays up.

alex-ramirez: OK, immediate mitigation: we should disable TRT fusion for the eu-west runtime pool to stop crashloops and let requests failover or degrade to CPU variant. Rolling restart with patched ARG/config change.

oncall-eric: I'm going to kick a canary rollout - patch deployment `redwood-runtime-eu` with env `TRT_FUSION=off` and scale down/up. Doing it on two nodes first. Will watch.

pagerduty-bot: ACTIONS: Incident created. Incident commander=alex-ramirez, scribe=maya-k, follow-ups assigned: runtime-ops (investigate kernel), eng-ml (model build variants), sre (host telemetry). PagerEscalation timer set to 12m.

trent: When patching, add the `podSpec` toleration for draining to avoid mass eviction across entire AZ. Also disable autoscaler briefly.

runtime-ops: Patch applied to canary pods. Logs: fusion disabled, containers healthy on canary nodes. Rolling patch scheduled.

alex-ramirez: Rolling patch in progress: 10% -> 30% -> 100% by AZ. Watching `CrashLoopBackOff` counts. If crash count drops proceed, otherwise revert.

maya-k: Dashboard update: error budget burn reduced from 42% to 8% in 10m after canary. We'll mark customer impact as limited but visible.

sre-jun: We're seeing node level OOM messages on two hosts prior to segfaults: `Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child`. Could be memory corruption causing explosion of allocations. Collecting core dumps now.

runtime-ops: Collected coredumps and minimal repro container. Uploading to artifact store: s3://redwood-incidents/3932104567/coredumps/. Will attach gdb backtrace.

alex-ramirez: For postmortem, we need: exact kernel + driver versions, CUDA/driver traces, TensorRT version, and the model compile config. Also test whether running with `TF32=False` or quantized kernels changes repro.

maya-k: Handoff: i'm on to runbook phase 2. If the rolling patch completes without regression, move to mitigation stable and open an incident postmortem. If crash persists, escalation to eng-runtime for hotpatching the kernel.

oncall-eric: Rolling to 100% complete — crashloops dropped to near zero in eu-west. Some pods are still flapping in az-a-3 (3 hosts). I'm cordoning two suspect hosts and moving workloads off them.

trent: Cordoning hosts is good. Let's also check for ECC / hardware errors. `sudo dmesg | grep -i ecc` and run `nvidia-smi -q` on the suspect machines.

sre-jun: dmesg on host-az-a-3: repeated machine check exceptions and nvlink errors. Support ticket opened with provider for hardware replacement. Mark those hosts as degraded.

customer-success-lee: letting the affected customers know we've mitigated and are doing deeper root cause. They asked for temporary region failover — advise them to use global endpoint which will route to other regions; CS will coordinate. :thumbsup:

runtime-ops: Forensics: backtrace shows crash in custom fused attention kernel in vLLM when sequence length > 2048 and certain memory alignment triggers vectorized path. We suspect a corner-case in our custom kernel's bounds check.

alex-ramirez: Next steps: (1) keep TRT fusion disabled in production eu-west for 24-48h, (2) eng-runtime to open a PR to add additional bounds checks and a safe fallback in fused kernel, (3) schedule rolling kernel tests across long-context repros, (4) postmortem with customer impact and timeline.

maya-k: Assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime (runtime-ops) ticket #INC-3932104567-RT to fix kernel + tests, eng-ml to recompile models with conservative flags, sre to replace two degraded hosts, cs to update customers.

oncall-eric: Handoff to night oncall in 2h — leave incident in mitigation state. If crashes reappear, wake me.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place, severity downgraded to sev3. Next update planned 2 hours or on status change.

alex-ramirez: Thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem timeline once we have full kernel traces and the PR diff.

customer-success-lee: customers acknowledged and appreciate quick mitigation. Closing loop after postmortem.
